rulings.decision: Clipboard capture keeps the Linux daemon queue with content-fingerprint dedupe (lastFingerprint); upstream's per-generation dedupe (repeatedGeneration) is not used because Klipper re-assertions arrive as new daemon events. Consequence: on Linux an identical copy made right after the previous one is still dropped, so upstream's 're-copy moves to top / re-adds a deleted item' only happens when some other copy came in between.

OCR model hash check dropped (sync hashing). Upstream verifies the SHA-256 of eng/tur .traineddata.gz with readFileSync+hash on the main thread before OCR; the Linux port keeps prepareOcrLanguages (async, any installed tessdata, system models gzip-compressed locally, so fixed hashes would not match). Trade-off: a corrupted or tampered model in ocr-models/ is not detected and OCR may fail or return garbage until that file is deleted. cacheMethod 'none' and async stale .traineddata removal are taken.
Default Linux screenshot folders, output.ownsFile suppression and --hidden login item stay; upstream's watcher error logging is added.
Linux daemon-socket monitor stays; it now calls the new optional ready() callback on connect.

The Windows update channel (windows-update.json, signed .exe installer) is disabled on Linux: no scheduler, notification, tray entries, check or install; the Updates tab says the Linux build updates from its own repository.
